translation_en: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us: Nafi‘ narrated to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for ‘araya to be sold by estimated measure.
Ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, with this chain, and he said: “to be taken according to its estimated amount.”

Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us; and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated it to me: Isma‘il narrated to us. Both reported from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, with this chain, that the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for selling ‘araya according to their estimated amount.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah al-Qa‘nabi narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Yahya, Ibn Sa‘id, from Bashir ibn Yasar, from some of the Messenger’s Companions from their community, including Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade selling fruit for dates and said: “That is usury; that is muzabanah.” But he granted a concession for selling one or two ‘ariyyah palm trees, allowing a household to take their estimated yield in dates so they could eat the fruit fresh.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Bashir ibn Yasar, from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, that they said: The Messenger of Allah granted a concession for selling an ‘ariyyah for its estimated amount in dates.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi ‘Umar all reported from al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say that Bashir ibn Yasar informed him, from some of the Messenger’s Companions from their community, that the Messenger of Allah forbade this and mentioned a report like Sulayman ibn Bilal’s from Yahya. Ishaq and Ibn al-Muthanna used the word “barter” instead of “usury”; Ibn Abi ‘Umar said “usury.”

‘Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Numayr narrated it to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Bashir ibn Yasar, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, from the Prophet, with a report like theirs.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, who narrated to me from Bashir ibn Yasar, the client of Banu Harithah, that Rafi‘ ibn Khadij and Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah told him the Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah—fruit exchanged for dates—except for owners of ‘araya, whom he permitted.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa‘nab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us; and Yahya ibn Yahya said: I asked Malik whether Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to him, from Abu Sufyan, the client of Ibn Abi Ahmad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah granted a concession for selling ‘araya by estimate for less than five wasqs, or for five. Dawud was uncertain, saying five or less than five. Malik said, “Yes.”

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah. Muzabanah is selling fruit for dates by measure, and selling grapes for raisins by measure.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, who informed him that ‘Abd Allah said the Prophet forbade muzabanah: selling the fruit of date palms for dates by measure, grapes for raisins by measure, and crops for wheat by measure.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, with this chain and a report like it.

Yahya ibn Ma‘in, Harun ibn ‘Abd Allah, and Husayn ibn ‘Isa narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah, which is selling date-palm fruit for dates by measure, raisins for grapes by measure, and any fruit for its estimated amount.

‘Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma‘il, Ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah. Muzabanah is selling the fruit on palm trees for a specified measure of dates, with any surplus going to me and any shortfall falling on me.
Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil narrated it to us: Hammad narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, with this chain and a report like it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah, who said the Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah: selling the fruit of one’s garden by measure for dates if it is palm trees, for raisins if it is grapevines, or for a measured amount of food if it is crops. He forbade all of that. Qutaybah’s narration says, “or if it is crops.”

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus informed me; Ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak informed me; and Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated it to me: Hafs ibn Mayसरah narrated to us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to me. All reported from Nafi‘ with this chain and a report like theirs.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever sells palm trees after they have been pollinated, their fruit belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us. Both reported from ‘Ubayd Allah; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his—Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Any palm trees whose roots are bought after they have been pollinated, their fruit belongs to the one who pollinated them, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet said: “Whoever pollinates palm trees and then sells their roots, their fruit belongs to the one who pollinated them, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.”

Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil narrated it to us: Hammad narrated to us; and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Isma‘il narrated to us. Both reported from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, with this chain and a report like it.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us; Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever buys palm trees after they have been pollinated, their fruit belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise. Whoever buys a slave, his property belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to us. Yahya said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us; the other two said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain and a report like it.

Harmalah ibn Yahya informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who told me that Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said his father said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say something like it.

Al-Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Abu Tawbah narrated to us: Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever has land should cultivate it or grant it to his brother. If he refuses, let him keep his land.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade muhaqalah and muzabanah.

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that Abu Sufyan, the client of Ibn Abi Ahmad, told him he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: The Messenger of Allah forbade muzabanah and muhaqalah. Muzabanah is buying fruit while it is still on palm trees; muhaqalah is leasing land.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu al-Rabi‘ al-‘Ataki narrated to us. Abu al-Rabi‘ said: He narrated to us; Yahya said: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from ‘Amr, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Umar say: We saw no harm in sharecropping until the first year, when Rafi‘ claimed that the Prophet of Allah had forbidden it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; ‘Ali ibn Hujr and Ibrahim ibn Dinar narrated to me: Isma‘il, Ibn ‘Ulayyah, narrated to us, from Ayyub; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Waki‘ narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us. All reported from ‘Amr ibn Dinar with this chain and a report like it. Ibn ‘Uyaynah’s hadith adds: “So we abandoned it because of him.”
‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to me: Isma‘il narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Khalil, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn ‘Umar said, “Rafi‘ deprived us of the benefit of our land.”
